name: Street Custom 'Sewer Rat' Underground Navigation Kit
product_name: Street Custom 'Sewer Rat' Underground Navigation Kit
description: A kit for navigating GLMZ's extensive underground infrastructure — storm drains, maintenance tunnels, abandoned transit lines, and DEAES tunnel networks. The kit includes a chemical light supply, waterproof map case with hand-copied tunnel charts, a gas detection badge that changes color in dangerous atmospheres, a compact rebreather for short exposures, and a sonic locator that maps tunnel geometry by echolocation. The Sewer Rat kit is the standard equipment of underground couriers, smugglers, and the growing population that lives beneath the city.
story_hooks: A Sewer Rat tunnel chart has been found that maps passages no official survey has documented — including one that passes directly beneath a high-security corporate vault.

Underground couriers using Sewer Rat kits have established a delivery network that is faster than surface transit for short distances — packages move through the tunnel system with no surveillance coverage.
related_entities: Dredge Mining Collective Deep Earth Autonomous Excavation System

physical_description.visual_profile: A weathered, modular shoulder bag with a utilitarian silhouette — boxy yet ergonomic, suggesting function over form. The exterior shows visible patching and reinforced stitching, with equipment pouches arranged for rapid access. It reads as rugged, purpose-built field gear that's been through heavy use in hostile environments.
physical_description.dimensions: 38 cm wide × 28 cm tall × 15 cm deep — backpack-sized, fits snugly across chest or shoulder
physical_description.weight_description: 2.5 kg loaded — handheld carrying strap with quick-release buckle, designed for balance during low-light navigation
physical_description.primary_material: Rubberized industrial canvas exterior with reinforced corner brackets; internal compartments feature waterproof thermoplastic dividers
physical_description.finish: Matte weathered texture with deliberate scuff marks and discoloration from moisture exposure. Seams sealed with visible thermoplastic welding. Zipper sliders show oxidation patina.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with acid-yellow safety trim along seams and pocket edges. Ink-black nylon webbing straps. Internal compartments line-marked in faded glow-in-the-dark paint.
physical_description.interface_elements: Five labeled zippered pockets (chemicals, maps, sensors, rebreather, tools). Gas detection badge clipped to front flap — circular, thumb-sized, with color gradient panel visible. Sonic locator mounted in quick-access side pouch with small LCD screen (2×2 cm). Main compartment contains waterproof map case (A5-sized laminated folder with hand-written tunnel annotations in blue ink).
distinctive_features: Integrated chemical light quiver — 20 slim glow-stick tubes visible through semi-transparent side panel
Gas badge color-change indicator: baseline gray, shifts to amber/red/purple depending on detected hazard type
Sonic locator displays radial sonar mapping on monochrome LCD — faint green phosphor glow
Hand-copied tunnel charts visible in case: amateur cartography with scrawled route notes, dead-ends marked with red X
Worn manufacturer patch (faded Street Custom logo) on front flap — stylized rat silhouette in reflective thread
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Street Custom woven label on interior flap; laser-etched serial number on zipper slider; regulatory water-rating symbol stamped near base (submersion rated 5 meters × 72 hours)
physical_description.condition_typical: Visual signs of field use — salt deposits around seams, faint algal staining on lower edge, chemical light adhesive residue on quiver panel. Zippers show minor corrosion. Map case corners show soft creasing from repeated unfolding. Overall impression: trusted, proven equipment of someone who spends significant time beneath the city.
